conventions.convention: The Hilbert inner product is linear in its first argument. Countable Choice is assumed, and the Hilbert space is nonzero.

The Minkowski pairing is p·a = p⁰a⁰ − p⃗·a⃗; the closed forward cone is p⁰ ≥ |p⃗|, and the open forward cone is b⁰ > |b⃗|. Translations use exp(ip·a), so future imaginary displacement gives exp(−p·b).

The joint PVM and its forward-cone support are separately assumed. Vacuum cyclicity does not imply uniqueness, and a separately specified local assignment carries no automatic locality, isotony or covariance.

Holomorphy uses a complex-linear total derivative on the full complex coordinate domain. Boundary continuity is strong operator continuity; insertions are bounded, with no conclusion for unbounded field products.
The CPT/spin-statistics interface is a checklist, not a sufficiency theorem. Field-domain, distributional continuation, complex-group continuation and boundary uniqueness obligations remain separate.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On a nonzero complex Hilbert space with first-variable-linear pairing, specify a strongly continuous unitary translation representation U and a Borel PVM E with U(a) = Φ_E(exp(ip·a)) and E(R⁴ ∖ closed forward cone) = 0, together with a translation-invariant unit vector Ω cyclic for a specified unital star-subalgebra of bounded operators.

Assume Countable Choice and the positive-energy joint spectral input. The cone-restricted spectral integral U(a+ib) is a contraction, extends strongly continuously to the closed future tube, and agrees with U(a) at b=0. For every integer n≥1, bounded insertions B₁,…,Bₙ₋₁ and vectors ψ,φ, the coefficient (U(z₁)B₁U(z₂)⋯Bₙ₋₁U(zₙ)ψ,φ) is holomorphic on the product of n open future tubes. No locality assumption is used, and no claim about unbounded Wightman fields is asserted.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicitly assumed choice principle carried into the Hilbert-adjoint and bounded PVM-integral suppliers.
First-variable linearity, conjugate symmetry and induced norm.
The complete complex inner-product spaces underlying the spectral input and field interface.
Bounded adjoints and their identities for the inherited unital star-algebra structure.
Normalized orthogonal projection values, their intersection product law and strong countable additivity.
Supporting the spectral-integral supplier through positive scalar measures and finite complex coefficient measures.
Supporting uniform simple-function construction of the bounded spectral integral.
Existence, uniqueness, pairing formula, norm bound and quadratic identity for bounded Borel spectral multipliers. Its nonzero-space and Countable Choice hypotheses are retained.
The test functions and seminorms used by the field interface and Poincaré pullback suppliers.
The precise topology underlying continuous test pullbacks and weakly tempered field coefficients.
Continuous complex-linear functionals on Schwartz space and the bilinear distribution/test pairing.
Minkowski signature, forward cone, spacelike separation, proper-orthochronous group and affine test pullback.
The unital complex star-algebra operations required of the bounded operator algebra.
Holomorphy defined by a complex-linear total derivative with a little-o remainder, rather than an unstated separate-holomorphy theorem.
Common invariant field domain and tempered scalar matrix coefficients, without claiming point fields or self-adjoint closures.
The algebraic tensor test algebra used in the pullback-continuity and reconstruction context.
Ensuring transformed tests remain Schwartz and the pullbacks are continuous.
Checking the remarks faithfully distinguish its conditional matrix-coefficient Fourier-support conclusion from the separately supplied joint PVM.

concerns.concern: The Definition contains inline links to [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]] and [[def-qft-involutive-algebra-state]]. SCHEMA.md requires uninterrupted definitions without hyperlinks, with links in Definition references. Both suppliers are legitimate prerequisites; this is an editorial placement defect.
The Statement opens with the inline link [[def-qftx-joint-spectrum-input]], despite the statement-first rule requiring links in Statement references. The hypothesis itself is appropriate.

The Álvarez-Gaumé/Vázquez-Mozo source locator describes a “bounded-insertion CPT proof interface.” The cited §4 instead discusses Wightman field distributions and their analytic continuation, with the noncommutative continuation restricted to electric coordinates; bounded insertions are supported by the separate Fewster/Rejzner citation. Correct this attribution without changing the sound local bounded-operator proof. Checked [§4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/0305093) and [Fewster/Rejzner §§5.1–5.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.04051). seams_checked.note: The page declares this prerequisite. Its scattering-approximant definition faithfully restates the joint PVM, Fourier sign, forward support and invariant cyclic vacuum. It separately introduces locality and isolated-shell hypotheses, and explicitly distinguishes cyclicity from vacuum uniqueness. The Cook and comparison-operator results do not infer their derivative estimates, inner-product limits or completeness from tube analyticity. Conversely, the supplier asserts no scattering conclusion.
